predecessors.name: Eastern Roman Empire
predecessors.text: the imperial possessions of the western Mediterranean under the praetorian prefect of Africa: 'all imperial possessions in the western Mediterranean'

successors.name: Umayyad Caliphate
successors.text: Carthage and Africa, 'the final end of Roman control and influence over Carthage, and subsequently all of North Africa' (Battle of Carthage page)

successors.name: Byzantine Empire
successors.text: Sardinia, listed in the infobox as 'Byzantine Sardinia', and (page silent) Corsica and the Balearics

ledger.x: 591: the exarchate is set up at Carthage.
624: the Visigoths take the last Byzantine outposts in Spain.
647: the Arabs invade the exarchate and meet Gregory at Sufetula.
648: the Arabs withdraw for a tribute.
697: Hasan ibn al-Nu'man invades the Byzantine coast.
698: the battle for Carthage ends the fighting.
698: Carthage falls and with it Byzantine Africa.
698: Sardinia stays with Constantinople as 'Byzantine Sardinia'.
698: Corsica and the Balearics leave the exarchate.

wars.name: Gregory's revolt and the Arab invasion of Ifriqiya (Battle of Sufetula)
wars.outcome: Gregory the Patrician rebelled against Constans II in 646, was defeated and killed at Sufetula in 647; the Arabs sacked Sufetula and raided the exarchate, then left in 648 for a tribute of 2,520,000 dinars, and Africa returned to imperial allegiance.

wars.name: Uqba ibn Nafi's campaign and the Battle of Vescera
wars.outcome: Uqba founded Kairouan in 670; in 683 (682 on the Exarchate page) he was ambushed 'by the Berber Christian king Kusaila and his Byzantine allies in the Battle of Vescera'.

wars.name: Umayyad conquest of Byzantine Africa
wars.outcome: A new army 'in 694... taking Carthage and ending the Byzantine presence by 698'; Hasan entered the capital 'unopposed in 695/6', a Byzantine fleet under John the Patrician briefly retook it, and the Battle of Carthage in 698 ended it.

certainty.note: Provincial and coastal holdings of the exarchate: no page gives a frontier; the Moorish interior and the 530s-540s Mauri wars are not on the pages opened.
